import Mathlib
import Logic.InformationGeometryLogPartition

/-!
# Kullback–Leibler divergence of a finite exponential family is a Bregman divergence

This file continues the information-geometry thread of
`Probability.InformationGeometryContrarian` and
`Logic.InformationGeometryLogPartition`.

Working with the finite exponential family
`expFamily q T θ x = q x * exp ⟪θ, T x⟫ / Z(θ)` of the previous file, we prove:

* `klDiv_expFamily_eq_bregman` — the exact identity
  `KL(p_θ ‖ p_η) = A(η) - A(θ) - ⟪η - θ, μ(θ)⟫`,
  i.e. the KL divergence *is* the Bregman divergence generated by the
  log-partition function `A`, with `μ = ∇A` the expectation parameters;
* `klDiv_nonneg` — Gibbs' inequality, proved from `log x ≤ x - 1`;
* `logPartition_tangent_le` — hence `A` lies above each of its tangent planes,
  so `μ(θ)` is a subgradient of `A` at `θ`;
* `logPartition_convexOn` — consequently `A` is convex on all of `ℝ^d`,
  a purely information-theoretic proof of convexity of the log-partition
  function that uses no second derivative;
* `symmetrized_kl_eq` and `meanParam_monotone` — the Jeffreys divergence equals
  `⟪η - θ, μ(η) - μ(θ)⟫`, so the mean-parameter map is a monotone operator;
* exact Bernoulli evidence (`bernoulli_meanParam_zero`, `bernoulli_fisher_zero`,
  `bernoulli_klDiv_exact`);
* a contrarian boundary result, `degenerate_klDiv_zero`: with a constant
  sufficient statistic, distinct natural parameters have zero KL divergence, so
  the Bregman/Legendre picture genuinely needs an identifiability assumption;
  the Fisher matrix is then identically zero (`degenerate_fisher_zero`).
-/

open Finset Real

namespace InformationGeometryBregman

open InformationGeometryContrarian InformationGeometryLogPartition

variable {S : Type*} [Fintype S] {d : ℕ}

/-! ## I. Kullback–Leibler divergence on finite probability vectors -/

/-- Kullback–Leibler divergence of two finite weight vectors. -/
def klDiv (p r : S → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ x, p x * Real.log (p x / r x)

/-- **Gibbs' inequality.** The KL divergence of two positive probability
vectors is nonnegative.  The proof is the classical `log x ≤ x - 1` argument. -/
theorem klDiv_nonneg {p r : S → ℝ} (hp : ∀ x, 0 < p x) (hr : ∀ x, 0 < r x)
    (hps : ∑ x, p x = 1) (hrs : ∑ x, r x = 1) : 0 ≤ klDiv p r := by
  have hbound : ∀ x, p x * Real.log (r x / p x) ≤ r x - p x := by
    intro x
    have hpx : p x ≠ 0 := (hp x).ne'
    have hlog : Real.log (r x / p x) ≤ r x / p x - 1 :=
      Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (div_pos (hr x) (hp x))
    have hmul := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hlog (le_of_lt (hp x))
    calc p x * Real.log (r x / p x) ≤ p x * (r x / p x - 1) := hmul
      _ = r x - p x := by field_simp
  have hsum : ∑ x, p x * Real.log (r x / p x) ≤ ∑ x, (r x - p x) :=
    Finset.sum_le_sum fun x _ => hbound x
  rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, hps, hrs, sub_self] at hsum
  have hneg : klDiv p r = -∑ x, p x * Real.log (r x / p x) := by

/-- **Fenchel–Young inequality** for the log-partition function. -/
theorem fenchel_young_le [Nonempty S] {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x) (θ η : Fin d → ℝ) :
    dotp θ (meanParam q T η) ≤ logPartition q T θ + dualPotential q T η := by
  have h := fenchel_young_eq T hq θ η
  have hnn := klDiv_expFamily_nonneg T hq η θ
  linarith

/-- Equality in Fenchel–Young holds exactly when the two family members
coincide as distributions. -/
theorem fenchel_young_eq_iff [Nonempty S] {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x) (θ η : Fin d → ℝ) :
    dotp θ (meanParam q T η) = logPartition q T θ + dualPotential q T η
      ↔ expFamily q T η = expFamily q T θ := by
  have hid := fenchel_young_eq T hq θ η
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_contra hne
    have hpos := klDiv_pos_of_ne (expFamily_pos T hq η) (expFamily_pos T hq θ)
      (expFamily_sum_one T hq η) (expFamily_sum_one T hq θ) hne
    linarith
  · intro h
    have hzero : klDiv (expFamily q T η) (expFamily q T θ) = 0 := by
      simp [klDiv, h]
    linarith

respect to the (normalized) base measure. -/
theorem dualPotential_eq_klDiv_base [Nonempty S] {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ)

  have hlog : ∀ x, expFamily q T θ x * Real.log (expFamily q T θ x / q x)
      = expFamily q T θ x * dotp θ (T x)
        - logPartition q T θ * expFamily q T θ x := by
    intro x
    rw [Real.log_div (expFamily_pos T hq θ x).ne' (hq x).ne',
      log_expFamily T hq θ x]
    ring
  rw [klDiv]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => hlog x, Finset.sum_sub_distrib,
    ← Finset.mul_sum, expFamily_sum_one T hq θ]
  rw [show (∑ x, expFamily q T θ x * dotp θ (T x)) = dotp θ (meanParam q T θ) from

  rw [dualPotential]

/-- **The mean map separates distinct distributions.**  If two members of the
family are distinct as probability vectors, their expectation parameters
differ.  This is the coordinate-change half of dual flatness: on an identifiable
family, natural and expectation coordinates are in bijection. -/
theorem meanParam_injective [Nonempty S] {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x) (θ η : Fin d → ℝ)
    (hne : expFamily q T θ ≠ expFamily q T η) :
    meanParam q T θ ≠ meanParam q T η := by
  intro hmean
  have hsym := symmetrized_kl_eq T hq θ η
  rw [hmean, sub_self] at hsym
  have h1 := klDiv_pos_of_ne (expFamily_pos T hq θ) (expFamily_pos T hq η)
    (expFamily_sum_one T hq θ) (expFamily_sum_one T hq η) hne
  have h2 := klDiv_expFamily_nonneg T hq η θ
  linarith

/-! ## III. The Fisher metric is the Hessian of relative entropy -/

omit [Fintype S] in
theorem dotp_add_smul_sub (θ v m : Fin d → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    dotp (θ + t • v - θ) m = t * dotp v m := by
  have h : θ + t • v - θ = t • v := by
    funext i; simp
  rw [h]
  simp only [dotp, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring

/-- Along an e-geodesic, relative entropy is the difference between the
log-partition function and its tangent plane. -/
theorem klDiv_along_egeodesic [Nonempty S] {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x) (θ v : Fin d → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    klDiv (expFamily q T θ) (expFamily q T (θ + t • v))
      = logPartition q T (θ + t • v) - logPartition q T θ
        - t * dotp v (meanParam q T θ) := by
  rw [klDiv_expFamily_eq_bregman T hq θ (θ + t • v), dotp_add_smul_sub]

/-- **First derivative of relative entropy along an e-geodesic.** -/
theorem hasDerivAt_klDiv_dir [Nonempty S] {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x) (θ v : Fin d → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t => klDiv (expFamily q T θ) (expFamily q T (θ + t • v)))
      (dotp v (meanParam q T (θ + t • v)) - dotp v (meanParam q T θ)) t := by
  have hfun : (fun t => klDiv (expFamily q T θ) (expFamily q T (θ + t • v)))
      = fun t => logPartition q T (θ + t • v)
        - (logPartition q T θ + t * dotp v (meanParam q T θ)) := by
    funext t
    rw [klDiv_along_egeodesic T hq θ v t]
    ring
  rw [hfun]
  have h1 := hasDerivAt_logPartition_dir T hq θ v t
  have h2 : HasDerivAt
      (fun t : ℝ => logPartition q T θ + t * dotp v (meanParam q T θ))
      (dotp v (meanParam q T θ)) t := by
    simpa using ((hasDerivAt_id t).mul_const (dotp v (meanParam q T θ))).const_add
      (logPartition q T θ)
  exact h1.sub h2

/-- Relative entropy is stationary at the base point of an e-geodesic: KL has a
vanishing first-order differential, so its leading behaviour is quadratic. -/
theorem klDiv_deriv_zero [Nonempty S] {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x) (θ v : Fin d → ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => klDiv (expFamily q T θ) (expFamily q T (θ + t • v)))
      0 (0 : ℝ) := by
  have h := hasDerivAt_klDiv_dir T hq θ v 0
  have hzero : θ + (0 : ℝ) • v = θ := by funext i; simp
  rw [hzero] at h
  simpa using h

/-- **The Fisher metric is the second-order differential of relative entropy.**
The second derivative along an e-geodesic is the Fisher quadratic form. -/
theorem hessian_klDiv_eq_fisher [Nonempty S] {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x) (θ v : Fin d → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt
      (fun t => dotp v (meanParam q T (θ + t • v)) - dotp v (meanParam q T θ))
      (∑ i, ∑ j, v i * featureFisher (expFamily q T (θ + t • v)) T i j * v j) t := by
  have h := hessian_logPartition_eq_fisher T hq θ v t
  simpa using h.sub_const (dotp v (meanParam q T θ))

/-- The second-order differential of KL at the base point is the Fisher matrix
of the family at that point. -/
theorem hessian_klDiv_at_zero [Nonempty S] {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x) (θ v : Fin d → ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt
      (fun t : ℝ => dotp v (meanParam q T (θ + t • v)) - dotp v (meanParam q T θ))
      (∑ i, ∑ j, v i * featureFisher (expFamily q T θ) T i j * v j) (0 : ℝ) := by
  have h := hessian_klDiv_eq_fisher T hq θ v 0
  have hzero : θ + (0 : ℝ) • v = θ := by funext i; simp
  rw [hzero] at h
  exact h

/-- Relative entropy along an e-geodesic has nonnegative second derivative,
hence is convex in the geodesic parameter. -/
theorem klDiv_second_deriv_nonneg [Nonempty S] {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x) (θ v : Fin d → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, v i * featureFisher (expFamily q T (θ + t • v)) T i j * v j :=
  featureFisher_positiveSemidefinite _ T
    (fun x => (expFamily_pos T hq (θ + t • v) x).le) v

/-!
# The log-partition function of a finite exponential family

This file closes the first "future direction" of
`Probability.InformationGeometryContrarian`: it connects the *abstract centered
feature model* used there (`featureFisher`, `scoreCubic`) with genuine
derivatives of a finite log-partition function.

For a finite sample space `S`, a positive base weight `q`, a sufficient
statistic `T : S → Fin d → ℝ` and a natural parameter `θ`, put

* `partitionFn q T θ = ∑ x, q x * exp ⟪θ, T x⟫`,
* `logPartition q T θ = log (partitionFn q T θ)`,
* `expFamily q T θ x = q x * exp ⟪θ, T x⟫ / partitionFn q T θ`,
* `meanParam q T θ i = 𝔼_{expFamily q T θ} [T · i]`.

The main results are the first three directional derivatives of the
log-partition function along a tangent vector `v`:

* `hasDerivAt_logPartition_dir` : `d/dt A(θ + t v) = ⟪v, μ(θ + t v)⟫`;
* `hessian_logPartition_eq_fisher` : `d²/dt² A(θ + t v)` is the Fisher

* `third_derivative_logPartition_eq_cubic` : `d³/dt³ A(θ + t v)` is the

  `scoreCubic (expFamily q T (θ + tv)) T`.

Everything is obtained from a single uniform lemma on exponentially tilted
moments: `d/dt mₖ(t) = mₖ₊₁(t) - mₖ(t) m₁(t)`.
-/

open Finset Real

namespace InformationGeometryLogPartition

variable {S : Type*} [Fintype S]

/-! ## I. Exponentially tilted moments of a scalar statistic -/

/-- The unnormalized `k`-th moment of `s` under the tilt `u x * exp (t * s x)`. -/
def momentSum (u s : S → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ x, u x * s x ^ k * Real.exp (t * s x)

/-- The tilted probability weights `u x * exp (t s x) / Z(t)`. -/
def tiltDensity (u s : S → ℝ) (t : ℝ) (x : S) : ℝ :=
  u x * Real.exp (t * s x) / momentSum u s 0 t

/-- The normalized `k`-th moment of `s` under the tilted weights. -/
def moment (u s : S → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  momentSum u s k t / momentSum u s 0 t

theorem momentSum_zero_eq (u s : S → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    momentSum u s 0 t = ∑ x, u x * Real.exp (t * s x) := by
  simp [momentSum]

  have h : ∀ x ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset S),

    funext t; simp [momentSum]
  rw [e]
  exact HasDerivAt.sum h

    simp only [pow_zero, mul_one]
    exact mul_pos (hu x) (Real.exp_pos _)) Finset.univ_nonempty

/-- Expanding the second central moment of a probability vector. -/

/-! ## III. Finite exponential families -/

variable {d : ℕ}

/-- Euclidean pairing of a parameter with a statistic value. -/
def dotp (θ v : Fin d → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ i, θ i * v i

/-- Unnormalized exponential family weights. -/
def expWeight (q : S → ℝ) (T : S → Fin d → ℝ) (θ : Fin d → ℝ) (x : S) : ℝ :=
  q x * Real.exp (dotp θ (T x))

/-- The partition function of a finite exponential family. -/
def partitionFn (q : S → ℝ) (T : S → Fin d → ℝ) (θ : Fin d → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ x, expWeight q T θ x

/-- The log-partition (cumulant generating) function. -/
def logPartition (q : S → ℝ) (T : S → Fin d → ℝ) (θ : Fin d → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Real.log (partitionFn q T θ)

/-- The exponential family probability vector at natural parameter `θ`. -/
def expFamily (q : S → ℝ) (T : S → Fin d → ℝ) (θ : Fin d → ℝ) (x : S) : ℝ :=
  expWeight q T θ x / partitionFn q T θ

/-- Expectation parameters (mean of the sufficient statistic). -/
def meanParam (q : S → ℝ) (T : S → Fin d → ℝ) (θ : Fin d → ℝ) (i : Fin d) : ℝ :=
  weightedExpectation (expFamily q T θ) (fun x => T x i)

theorem dotp_add_smul (θ v w : Fin d → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    dotp (θ + t • v) w = dotp θ w + t * dotp v w := by

/-- The one-parameter subfamily `θ + t v` is the exponential tilt of the base

    expWeight q T (θ + t • v) x

    partitionFn q T (θ + t • v)
      = momentSum (expWeight q T θ) (fun x => dotp v (T x)) 0 t := by

    expFamily q T (θ + t • v)

  funext x

theorem expWeight_pos {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ) (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x) (θ : Fin d → ℝ)
    (x : S) : 0 < expWeight q T θ x :=
  mul_pos (hq x) (Real.exp_pos _)

theorem partitionFn_pos [Nonempty S] {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ) (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x)
    (θ : Fin d → ℝ) : 0 < partitionFn q T θ :=
  Finset.sum_pos (fun x _ => expWeight_pos T hq θ x) Finset.univ_nonempty

theorem expFamily_pos [Nonempty S] {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ) (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x)
    (θ : Fin d → ℝ) (x : S) : 0 < expFamily q T θ x :=
  div_pos (expWeight_pos T hq θ x) (partitionFn_pos T hq θ)

    rw [partitionFn, Finset.sum_div]

/-! ## IV. Derivatives of the log-partition function -/

  rw [moment_eq_expectation, ← expFamily_add_smul]

/-- **First derivative.** The directional derivative of the log-partition

theorem hasDerivAt_logPartition_dir [Nonempty S] {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x) (θ v : Fin d → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t => logPartition q T (θ + t • v))

  have h := hasDerivAt_logMomentSum (u := expWeight q T θ) (fun x => dotp v (T x)) hu t

    (h1 : ∑ x, p1 x = 1) (h2 : ∑ y, p2 y = 1) :
    ∑ z, prodWeights p1 p2 z = 1 := by
  have h := weightedExpectation_prod p1 p2 (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))
  rw [weightedExpectation_one h1, weightedExpectation_one h2] at h
  simpa [weightedExpectation] using h

omit [Fintype S] [Fintype S'] in
theorem prodWeights_pos {p1 : S → ℝ} {p2 : S' → ℝ}
    (h1 : ∀ x, 0 < p1 x) (h2 : ∀ y, 0 < p2 y) (z : S × S') :
    0 < prodWeights p1 p2 z :=
  mul_pos (h1 z.1) (h2 z.2)

/-! ## II. Central moments of independent sums -/

/-- The mean of a sum of independent observables. -/
theorem weightedExpectation_prod_add {p1 : S → ℝ} {p2 : S' → ℝ} (f : S → ℝ) (g : S' → ℝ)
    (h1 : ∑ x, p1 x = 1) (h2 : ∑ y, p2 y = 1) :
    weightedExpectation (prodWeights p1 p2) (fun z => f z.1 + g z.2)
      = weightedExpectation p1 f + weightedExpectation p2 g := by
  have hsplit : (fun z : S × S' => f z.1 + g z.2)
      = fun z : S × S' => f z.1 * (1 : ℝ) + (1 : ℝ) * g z.2 := by
    funext z; ring
  rw [hsplit, weightedExpectation_add,
    weightedExpectation_prod p1 p2 f (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)),
    weightedExpectation_prod p1 p2 (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) g,
    weightedExpectation_one h1, weightedExpectation_one h2]
  ring

/-- **Variances add** for independent observables. -/
theorem centralSecond_prod {p1 : S → ℝ} {p2 : S' → ℝ} (f : S → ℝ) (g : S' → ℝ)
    (h1 : ∑ x, p1 x = 1) (h2 : ∑ y, p2 y = 1) :
    weightedExpectation (prodWeights p1 p2)
        (fun z => (f z.1 + g z.2
          - weightedExpectation (prodWeights p1 p2) (fun w => f w.1 + g w.2)) ^ 2)
      = weightedExpectation p1 (fun x => (f x - weightedExpectation p1 f) ^ 2)
        + weightedExpectation p2 (fun y => (g y - weightedExpectation p2 g) ^ 2) := by
  set a : S → ℝ := fun x => f x - weightedExpectation p1 f with ha
  set b : S' → ℝ := fun y => g y - weightedExpectation p2 g with hb
  have hmean := weightedExpectation_prod_add (p1 := p1) (p2 := p2) f g h1 h2
  have hrw : (fun z : S × S' => (f z.1 + g z.2
      - weightedExpectation (prodWeights p1 p2) (fun w => f w.1 + g w.2)) ^ 2)
      = fun z : S × S' => a z.1 ^ 2 * (1 : ℝ)
        + ((2 * a z.1) * b z.2 + (1 : ℝ) * b z.2 ^ 2) := by
    funext z
    rw [hmean, ha, hb]
    ring
  rw [hrw, weightedExpectation_add, weightedExpectation_add,
    weightedExpectation_prod p1 p2 (fun x => a x ^ 2) (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)),
    weightedExpectation_prod p1 p2 (fun x => 2 * a x) b,
    weightedExpectation_prod p1 p2 (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) (fun y => b y ^ 2),
    weightedExpectation_one h1, weightedExpectation_one h2]
  have hb0 : weightedExpectation p2 b = 0 := weightedExpectation_centered p2 g h2
  rw [hb0]
  ring

/-- **Third central moments add** for independent observables: the cubic
cumulant tensorizes. -/
theorem centralThird_prod {p1 : S → ℝ} {p2 : S' → ℝ} (f : S → ℝ) (g : S' → ℝ)
    (h1 : ∑ x, p1 x = 1) (h2 : ∑ y, p2 y = 1) :
    weightedExpectation (prodWeights p1 p2)
        (fun z => (f z.1 + g z.2
          - weightedExpectation (prodWeights p1 p2) (fun w => f w.1 + g w.2)) ^ 3)
      = weightedExpectation p1 (fun x => (f x - weightedExpectation p1 f) ^ 3)
        + weightedExpectation p2 (fun y => (g y - weightedExpectation p2 g) ^ 3) := by
  set a : S → ℝ := fun x => f x - weightedExpectation p1 f with ha
  set b : S' → ℝ := fun y => g y - weightedExpectation p2 g with hb
  have hmean := weightedExpectation_prod_add (p1 := p1) (p2 := p2) f g h1 h2
  have hrw : (fun z : S × S' => (f z.1 + g z.2
      - weightedExpectation (prodWeights p1 p2) (fun w => f w.1 + g w.2)) ^ 3)
      = fun z : S × S' => a z.1 ^ 3 * (1 : ℝ)
        + ((3 * a z.1 ^ 2) * b z.2
          + ((3 * a z.1) * b z.2 ^ 2 + (1 : ℝ) * b z.2 ^ 3)) := by
    funext z
    rw [hmean, ha, hb]
    ring
  rw [hrw, weightedExpectation_add, weightedExpectation_add, weightedExpectation_add,
    weightedExpectation_prod p1 p2 (fun x => a x ^ 3) (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)),
    weightedExpectation_prod p1 p2 (fun x => 3 * a x ^ 2) b,
    weightedExpectation_prod p1 p2 (fun x => 3 * a x) (fun y => b y ^ 2),
    weightedExpectation_prod p1 p2 (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) (fun y => b y ^ 3),
    weightedExpectation_one h1, weightedExpectation_one h2]
  have ha0 : weightedExpectation p1 a = 0 := weightedExpectation_centered p1 f h1
  have hb0 : weightedExpectation p2 b = 0 := weightedExpectation_centered p2 g h2
  rw [weightedExpectation_const_mul p1 a 3, ha0, hb0]
  ring

/-! ## III. The product exponential family -/

omit [Fintype S] [Fintype S'] in
theorem dotp_prodStat (T1 : S → Fin d → ℝ) (T2 : S' → Fin d → ℝ)
    (v : Fin d → ℝ) (z : S × S') :
    dotp v (prodStat T1 T2 z) = dotp v (T1 z.1) + dotp v (T2 z.2) := by
  simp only [dotp, prodStat, mul_add]
  exact Finset.sum_add_distrib

/-- The partition function of independent data factorizes. -/
theorem partitionFn_prod (q1 : S → ℝ) (q2 : S' → ℝ) (T1 : S → Fin d → ℝ)
    (T2 : S' → Fin d → ℝ) (θ : Fin d → ℝ) :
    partitionFn (prodWeights q1 q2) (prodStat T1 T2) θ
      = partitionFn q1 T1 θ * partitionFn q2 T2 θ := by
  have h := weightedExpectation_prod q1 q2 (fun x => Real.exp (dotp θ (T1 x)))
    (fun y => Real.exp (dotp θ (T2 y)))
  simp only [weightedExpectation] at h
  simp only [partitionFn, expWeight]
  rw [show (∑ z, prodWeights q1 q2 z * Real.exp (dotp θ (prodStat T1 T2 z)))
      = ∑ z, prodWeights q1 q2 z *
          (Real.exp (dotp θ (T1 z.1)) * Real.exp (dotp θ (T2 z.2))) from
    Finset.sum_congr rfl fun z _ => by rw [dotp_prodStat, Real.exp_add]]
  exact h

/-- **The log-partition function is additive over independent data.** -/
theorem logPartition_prod [Nonempty S] [Nonempty S'] {q1 : S → ℝ} {q2 : S' → ℝ}
    (T1 : S → Fin d → ℝ) (T2 : S' → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq1 : ∀ x, 0 < q1 x) (hq2 : ∀ y, 0 < q2 y) (θ : Fin d → ℝ) :
    logPartition (prodWeights q1 q2) (prodStat T1 T2) θ
      = logPartition q1 T1 θ + logPartition q2 T2 θ := by
  rw [logPartition, partitionFn_prod, Real.log_mul (partitionFn_pos T1 hq1 θ).ne'
    (partitionFn_pos T2 hq2 θ).ne']
  rfl

/-- The product exponential family is the product of the factor families. -/
theorem expFamily_prod [Nonempty S] [Nonempty S'] {q1 : S → ℝ} {q2 : S' → ℝ}
    (T1 : S → Fin d → ℝ) (T2 : S' → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq1 : ∀ x, 0 < q1 x) (hq2 : ∀ y, 0 < q2 y) (θ : Fin d → ℝ) :
    expFamily (prodWeights q1 q2) (prodStat T1 T2) θ
      = prodWeights (expFamily q1 T1 θ) (expFamily q2 T2 θ) := by
  funext z
  have hz1 := (partitionFn_pos T1 hq1 θ).ne'
  have hz2 := (partitionFn_pos T2 hq2 θ).ne'
  simp only [expFamily, expWeight, prodWeights, partitionFn_prod, dotp_prodStat,
    Real.exp_add]
  field_simp

/-! ## IV. Tensorization of the Fisher form and of the cubic tensor -/

theorem fisher_contract_eq_centralSecond (p : S → ℝ) (T : S → Fin d → ℝ) (v : Fin d → ℝ) :
    (∑ i, ∑ j, v i * featureFisher p T i j * v j)
      = weightedExpectation p (fun x =>
          (dotp v (T x) - weightedExpectation p (fun y => dotp v (T y))) ^ 2) := by
  rw [featureFisher_quadForm]
  exact congrArg (weightedExpectation p)
    (funext fun x => by rw [← centeredScore, centeredScore_eq])

theorem cubic_contract_eq_centralThird' (p : S → ℝ) (T : S → Fin d → ℝ) (v : Fin d → ℝ) :
    (∑ i, ∑ j, ∑ k, v i * v j * v k * scoreCubic p T i j k)
      = weightedExpectation p (fun x =>
          (dotp v (T x) - weightedExpectation p (fun y => dotp v (T y))) ^ 3) := by
  rw [cubic_contract_eq_centralThird]
  exact congrArg (weightedExpectation p)
    (funext fun x => by rw [centeredScore_eq])

/-- **Fisher information adds over independent data** (contracted form). -/
theorem fisher_contract_prod [Nonempty S] [Nonempty S'] {q1 : S → ℝ} {q2 : S' → ℝ}
    (T1 : S → Fin d → ℝ) (T2 : S' → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq1 : ∀ x, 0 < q1 x) (hq2 : ∀ y, 0 < q2 y) (θ v : Fin d → ℝ) :
    (∑ i, ∑ j, v i * featureFisher
        (expFamily (prodWeights q1 q2) (prodStat T1 T2) θ) (prodStat T1 T2) i j * v j)
      = (∑ i, ∑ j, v i * featureFisher (expFamily q1 T1 θ) T1 i j * v j)
        + (∑ i, ∑ j, v i * featureFisher (expFamily q2 T2 θ) T2 i j * v j) := by
  have h1 : ∑ x, expFamily q1 T1 θ x = 1 := expFamily_sum_one T1 hq1 θ
  have h2 : ∑ y, expFamily q2 T2 θ y = 1 := expFamily_sum_one T2 hq2 θ
  rw [fisher_contract_eq_centralSecond, fisher_contract_eq_centralSecond,
    fisher_contract_eq_centralSecond, expFamily_prod T1 T2 hq1 hq2 θ]
  simp only [dotp_prodStat]
  exact centralSecond_prod (p1 := expFamily q1 T1 θ) (p2 := expFamily q2 T2 θ)
    (fun x => dotp v (T1 x)) (fun y => dotp v (T2 y)) h1 h2

/-- **The Amari–Chentsov cubic tensor adds over independent data** (contracted
form).  This is the third-order analogue of Fisher additivity. -/
theorem cubic_contract_prod [Nonempty S] [Nonempty S'] {q1 : S → ℝ} {q2 : S' → ℝ}
    (T1 : S → Fin d → ℝ) (T2 : S' → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq1 : ∀ x, 0 < q1 x) (hq2 : ∀ y, 0 < q2 y) (θ v : Fin d → ℝ) :
    (∑ i, ∑ j, ∑ k, v i * v j * v k * scoreCubic
        (expFamily (prodWeights q1 q2) (prodStat T1 T2) θ) (prodStat T1 T2) i j k)
      = (∑ i, ∑ j, ∑ k, v i * v j * v k * scoreCubic (expFamily q1 T1 θ) T1 i j k)
        + (∑ i, ∑ j, ∑ k, v i * v j * v k * scoreCubic (expFamily q2 T2 θ) T2 i j k) := by
  have h1 : ∑ x, expFamily q1 T1 θ x = 1 := expFamily_sum_one T1 hq1 θ
  have h2 : ∑ y, expFamily q2 T2 θ y = 1 := expFamily_sum_one T2 hq2 θ
  rw [cubic_contract_eq_centralThird', cubic_contract_eq_centralThird',
    cubic_contract_eq_centralThird', expFamily_prod T1 T2 hq1 hq2 θ]
  simp only [dotp_prodStat]
  exact centralThird_prod (p1 := expFamily q1 T1 θ) (p2 := expFamily q2 T2 θ)
    (fun x => dotp v (T1 x)) (fun y => dotp v (T2 y)) h1 h2

/-- **Two-sample i.i.d. doubling law for the cubic tensor**, the third-order
counterpart of `G₂ = 2 G₁`. -/
theorem cubic_contract_iid_two [Nonempty S] {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x) (θ v : Fin d → ℝ) :
    (∑ i, ∑ j, ∑ k, v i * v j * v k * scoreCubic
        (expFamily (prodWeights q q) (prodStat T T) θ) (prodStat T T) i j k)
      = 2 * ∑ i, ∑ j, ∑ k, v i * v j * v k * scoreCubic (expFamily q T θ) T i j k := by
  rw [cubic_contract_prod T T hq hq θ v]
  ring

/-- Two-sample i.i.d. doubling law for the Fisher form. -/
theorem fisher_contract_iid_two [Nonempty S] {q : S → ℝ} (T : S → Fin d → ℝ)
    (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x) (θ v : Fin d → ℝ) :
    (∑ i, ∑ j, v i * featureFisher
        (expFamily (prodWeights q q) (prodStat T T) θ) (prodStat T T) i j * v j)
      = 2 * ∑ i, ∑ j, v i * featureFisher (expFamily q T θ) T i j * v j := by
  rw [fisher_contract_prod T T hq hq θ v]
  ring

end InformationGeometryTensorization

# Computational evidence

Cycle 1 of the information-geometry thread. The claims that mattered were tested
numerically before formalization; every number in the final tables is now also a
kernel-checked Lean theorem or an exact rational `#eval`.

## 1. Small-case calculations: the two-point exponential family

Base measure uniform on `{0,1}`, sufficient statistic `T = 1{x = 1}`, natural
parameter `θ`. Then

```
A(θ) = log(1 + e^θ),   μ(θ) = e^θ / (1 + e^θ),
A''  = μ(1 - μ),       A''' = μ(1 - μ)(1 - 2μ).
```

Exact rational values of the second and third *central* moments of a Bernoulli
law with success probability `p`, computed two ways (closed formula and direct
summation over the two outcomes; the two agree exactly, difference `0`):

| p | variance = Fisher | third central moment = Amari–Chentsov C |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1/4 | 3/16 | 3/32 |
| 1/2 | 1/4 | 0 |
| 1/3 | 2/9 | 2/27 |
| 3/4 | 3/16 | -3/32 |
| 1/5 | 4/25 | 12/125 |

Observations that shaped the formal development:

* the third cumulant vanishes exactly at the symmetric point `p = 1/2`, so any
  claim of the form "the cubic tensor is nonzero" must fix an *asymmetric*
  member; `p = 1/4` (natural parameter `θ★ = log(1/3)`) is the smallest
  convenient witness and is the one already used in the catalog's contrarian
  file;
* `C` changes sign under `p ↦ 1 - p`, matching the odd symmetry of a third
  central moment: a useful sanity check on the sign conventions in
  `scoreCubic`.

Both entries of the `p = 1/4` row are now theorems:
`InformationGeometryCubicEvidence.quarter_fisher_exact` (`3/16`) and
`quarter_cubic_exact` (`3/32`), and they are identified with genuine derivatives
of `A` in `quarter_second_derivative` and `quarter_third_derivative`.

## 2. Counterexample hunt

Three universal statements were stress-tested before being formalized.

* *"KL divergence between distinct natural parameters is positive."* **False.**
  Take the constant sufficient statistic `T ≡ 0`: the family is constant in `θ`,
  so `KL = 0` for all `θ ≠ η`. Formalized as
  `InformationGeometryBregman.degenerate_klDiv_zero`, together with
  `degenerate_fisher_zero`. The corrected statement, proved in
  `InformationGeometryLegendre.meanParam_injective`, conditions on the
  distributions being distinct rather than the parameters.

* *"The log-partition function is strictly convex."* **False** for the same
  reason (`degenerate_logPartition_const`). Only plain convexity is
  unconditionally true; that is what `logPartition_convexOn` states.

* *"The matrix Cramér–Rao bound needs an invertible Fisher matrix."* **Not
  needed.** In the efficient-direction formulation `b = G w`, the case
  `wᵀGw = 0` is covered by nonnegativity of the variance, so
  `cramer_rao_matrix` carries no invertibility hypothesis.

## 3. No integer sequence

All quantities produced here are rationals whose numerators and denominators
depend on the chosen Bernoulli parameter; no canonical integer sequence arises,
so an OEIS search is not applicable.

This closes the first "future direction" of the previous cycle: the abstract centered feature model is now identified with genuine derivatives of a log-partition function.

**`InformationGeometryBregman.lean`** — `KL(p_θ‖p_η) = A(η) − A(θ) − ⟪η−θ, μ(θ)⟫` (KL *is* the Bregman divergence of `A`), Gibbs' inequality and its strict form, convexity of `A` on all of ℝᵈ derived from relative entropy alone, the Jeffreys identity and monotonicity of the mean map, exact Bernoulli values, and a boundary counterexample: with a constant sufficient statistic distinct parameters have zero KL and vanishing Fisher matrix, so identifiability is indispensable.

# Future directions

Derived from cycle 1 of the information-geometry thread. This cycle added five
Lean files under `Catalog/Logic/`:

* `InformationGeometryLogPartition.lean` — the finite exponential family, and the
  first three directional derivatives of its log-partition function: gradient is
  the mean map, Hessian is the Fisher matrix, third derivative is the
  Amari–Chentsov cubic tensor;
* `InformationGeometryBregman.lean` — `KL = Bregman divergence of A`, Gibbs'
  inequality (with strict form), convexity of `A` proved from relative entropy
  alone, monotonicity of the mean map, and the degenerate boundary example;
* `InformationGeometryPythagoras.lean` — the three-point identity, Amari's
  generalized Pythagorean theorem, the projection inequality, and the matrix
  (efficient-direction) Cramér–Rao bound with its equality case;
* `InformationGeometryLegendre.lean` — Fenchel–Young duality, the dual potential
  as relative entropy to the base measure, injectivity of the mean map, and the
  Fisher metric as the Hessian of KL;
* `InformationGeometryCubicEvidence.lean` — the exact `3/16` and `3/32` Bernoulli
  numbers realized as honest derivatives of a log-partition function;
* `InformationGeometryTensorization.lean` — additivity of the log-partition
  function over independent data and the resulting additivity of the contracted
  Amari–Chentsov cubic tensor (`C₂ = 2 C₁`).

Each conjecture below is falsifiable and stated so that a single Lean file could
settle it.

## Conjecture 1 (dual flatness as a genuine coordinate change)

For an identifiable finite exponential family, the mean map
`μ : ℝ^d → interior(conv{T x})` is a bijection onto the interior of the convex
hull of the sufficient-statistic values, and the dual potential
`Ψ(μ) = ⟪θ(μ), μ⟫ - A(θ(μ))` satisfies `∇Ψ = θ` and
`KL(p_θ ‖ p_η) = Ψ(μ(θ)) - Ψ(μ(η)) - ⟪θ(η), μ(θ) - μ(η)⟫`, the Bregman
divergence of `Ψ` with arguments swapped.

*The key insight is* that this cycle already produced both halves of the
Legendre correspondence separately — injectivity of `μ` from strict Gibbs, and
surjectivity onto the interior from the fact that `A` is convex with the mean
map as its gradient — so what remains is an open-mapping / coercivity argument
rather than any new probabilistic content.

*Why now?* `meanParam_injective`, `logPartition_convexOn` and
`hasDerivAt_logPartition_dir` are formalized, and Mathlib's convex analysis
(`ConvexOn`, `interior (convexHull ℝ s)`) supplies the missing topology.

## Conjecture 2 (curvature, not just vanishing coefficients)

Define the alpha-connection of a finite exponential family as an actual
covariant derivative on the natural-parameter chart, with Christoffel symbols
obtained by raising an index of `((1 - α)/2) C` with the inverse Fisher matrix.
Then its Riemann curvature tensor vanishes identically for `α = ±1` and, for a
generic family with nonzero cubic tensor, is nonzero for every `α` with
`|α| ≠ 1`.

*The key insight is* that the contrarian file's counterexample shows flatness is
a property of the canonical construction rather than of the label `α`, and that
the honest way to make this precise is curvature: a coefficient-level statement
can always be broken by choosing a different connection with the same tag.

*Why now?* The cubic tensor is now available as a third derivative of `A`
(`third_derivative_logPartition_eq_cubic`), so the Christoffel symbols are
definable from analytic data instead of being postulated.

## Conjecture 3 (equality in Cramér–Rao characterizes exponential families)

For a `GenStatModel` with positive-definite Fisher matrix, equality
`Var(f) = wᵀ G w` in `cramer_rao_matrix` holds if and only if `f` is almost
surely affine in the directional score `w·score`; and if equality holds at every
parameter for a fixed statistic, the model is an exponential family with `f` as
sufficient statistic.

*The key insight is* that the forward direction is the Cauchy–Schwarz equality
case (a finite-dimensional statement already within reach), while the converse
is the classical characterization theorem and would need only the equality-case
lemma plus an integration of the score equation.

*Why now?* One direction is proved (`cramer_rao_equality_of_efficient`); the
missing converse is precisely the equality case of the weighted Cauchy–Schwarz
inequality already used in the catalog's `FisherCramerRao`.

## Conjecture 4 (Pythagorean projection exists and is unique)

Let `E` be a finite exponential family and `M` the set of members whose
expectation parameters satisfy a fixed affine constraint `⟪a, μ⟫ = c`. Then the
KL projection of a given `p_θ` onto `M` exists, is unique, and is characterized
by the orthogonality condition of `generalized_pythagoras`; moreover the
projection is the maximum-entropy member of `M` relative to the base measure.

*The key insight is* that this cycle proved the projection *inequality* from
orthogonality; the missing ingredient is only existence, i.e. compactness of the
constraint set in mean coordinates plus continuity of KL.

*Why now?* `projection_variational_strict` gives uniqueness for free once
existence is known, and `dualPotential_eq_klDiv_base` identifies the objective
with relative entropy to the base measure, which is the maximum-entropy
functional.

## Conjecture 5 (quantitative Pinsker in the exponential chart)

For a finite exponential family with Fisher matrix bounded below by `m > 0` and
above by `L` along a segment, the relative entropy along an e-geodesic obeys
`(m/2) t² ≤ KL(p_θ ‖ p_{θ + t v}) ≤ (L/2) t²` for `‖v‖ = 1`, and consequently a
two-sided Pinsker-type comparison between KL and total variation holds with
constants depending only on `m` and `L`.

*The key insight is* that with `klDiv_deriv_zero` and `hessian_klDiv_eq_fisher`
in hand, KL along an e-geodesic is a one-dimensional function with zero value and
zero derivative at the origin whose second derivative is exactly the Fisher form,
so the entire statement reduces to a Taylor bound in one real variable.

*Why now?* Both derivative facts are formalized in
`InformationGeometryLegendre.lean`, and Mathlib's
`Convex.inner_smul_le_norm_mul_norm` / mean-value machinery covers the remaining
step.

## Three concrete next-cycle sub-conjectures

1. `A` restricted to a line is strictly convex as soon as the Fisher form is
   positive in that direction at one point of the line.
2. The dual potential `Ψ` is convex as a function of the mean parameters, with
   `Ψ`-Bregman divergence equal to reversed KL.
3. The contracted form of this scaling law is now proved
   (`cubic_contract_prod`, `cubic_contract_iid_two`); what remains is the
   uncontracted tensor identity `C^{(1,2)}_{ijk} = C^{(1)}_{ijk} + C^{(2)}_{ijk}`
   and its `n`-fold iterate `C_n = n · C_1` for every `n`, by induction on the
   number of independent factors.

import Mathlib

/-!
# Langlands functoriality, I: Satake parameters, Hecke eigenvalues and local L-factors

This file develops, over an arbitrary commutative ring, the algebraic skeleton of the
local theory that underlies the Langlands program for `GL(2)`:

* the **Satake parameters** `(a, b)` of an unramified local representation of `GL(2)`;
* the associated **Hecke eigenvalue sequence** `hecke a b k` (the coefficient of the local
  L-function at `p ^ k`), defined by the classical degree-two recursion
  `a_{p^{k+2}} = a_p * a_{p^{k+1}} - χ(p) * a_{p^k}`;
* the **local L-function** as a formal power series, and the fact that it is the inverse of
  the degree-two Euler factor `(1 - a X)(1 - b X)`;
* the **Clebsch–Gordan / Hecke multiplicativity** identity
  `h_{n+d} * h_n = ∑_{i ≤ n} (ab)^{n-i} h_{d + 2i}`,
  which is the Satake-parameter shadow of the decomposition
  `Sym^m ⊗ Sym^n = ⊕_j Sym^{m+n-2j} ⊗ det^j`, and hence the local engine of functoriality;
* the **Ramanujan bound** `‖h_k‖ ≤ k + 1` for tempered (unitary) Satake parameters.

The general power-series lemma `PowerSeriesRecursion.mk_mul_eulerFactor` records the exact
equivalence "linear recursion of Hecke eigenvalues ↔ rationality of the local L-series with
prescribed Euler factor"; it is the workhorse for the `GL(3)` and `GL(4)` transfers in
`LanglandsSymmetricPower.lean`.
-/

namespace Langlands

open Finset PowerSeries

section PowerSeriesTools

variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R]

/-- Coefficient of `mk u * (C c * X ^ j)`: a shifted, scaled coefficient of `u`. -/
lemma coeff_mk_mul_CX (u : ℕ → R) (c : R) (j m : ℕ) :
    coeff m (PowerSeries.mk u * (C c * X ^ j)) = if j ≤ m then c * u (m - j) else 0 := by
  rw [show PowerSeries.mk u * (C c * X ^ j) = (C c * PowerSeries.mk u) * X ^ j by ring,
    coeff_mul_X_pow']
  split <;> simp

/-- Coefficient of a monomial `C a * X ^ j`. -/
lemma coeff_CX (a : R) (j m : ℕ) : coeff m (C a * X ^ j) = if m = j then a else 0 := by
  rw [coeff_C_mul, coeff_X_pow]; split <;> simp

/-- **Rationality from a linear recursion.**  If the sequence `u` satisfies the linear
recursion whose characteristic polynomial has coefficients `e 0, …, e d`, then the generating
series `∑ u k X ^ k` multiplied by the Euler factor `∑_{j ≤ d} e j X ^ j` is a polynomial of
degree `< d`, with explicitly computed coefficients.  This is the formal statement that a
local L-function is the reciprocal of a polynomial of degree `d`. -/
theorem mk_mul_eulerFactor (u : ℕ → R) (e : ℕ → R) (d : ℕ) (B : ℕ → R)
    (hB : ∀ m, B m = ∑ j ∈ range (m + 1), e j * u (m - j))
    (hrec : ∀ k, ∑ j ∈ range (d + 1), e j * u (k + d - j) = 0) :
    PowerSeries.mk u * (∑ j ∈ range (d + 1), C (e j) * X ^ j)
      = ∑ m ∈ range d, C (B m) * X ^ m := by
  ext m
  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  simp only [map_sum, coeff_mk_mul_CX, coeff_CX]
  by_cases hm : m < d
  · -- low-degree coefficients: both sides are the truncated convolution
    have hR : ∑ m' ∈ range d, (if m = m' then B m' else 0) = B m := by
      rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq (range d) m B, if_pos (Finset.mem_range.mpr hm)]
    have hL : ∑ j ∈ range (d + 1), (if j ≤ m then e j * u (m - j) else 0) = B m := by
      have hcast : ∀ j ∈ range (d + 1), (if j ≤ m then e j * u (m - j) else 0)
          = if j ∈ range (m + 1) then e j * u (m - j) else 0 := by
        intro j _
        simp
      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hcast, Finset.sum_ite_mem,
        Finset.inter_eq_right.mpr (by
          intro x hx
          simp only [Finset.mem_range] at hx ⊢
          omega), hB]
    rw [hL, hR]
  · -- high-degree coefficients: the recursion makes them vanish
    push_neg at hm
    have hzero : ∑ j ∈ range (d + 1), (if j ≤ m then e j * u (m - j) else 0) = 0 := by
      have hshift : ∀ j ∈ range (d + 1), (if j ≤ m then e j * u (m - j) else 0)
          = e j * u ((m - d) + d - j) := by
        intro j hj
        have hjd : j ≤ d := Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp (Finset.mem_range.mp hj)
        have hjm : j ≤ m := le_trans hjd hm
        rw [if_pos hjm, Nat.sub_add_cancel hm]
      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hshift]
      exact hrec (m - d)
    rw [hzero, Finset.sum_eq_zero]
    intro m' hm'
    have hne : ¬ (m = m') := by
      have := Finset.mem_range.mp hm'
      omega
    simp [hne]

/-- Rationality of a local L-series attached to a degree-two linear recursion. -/
theorem mk_mul_quadratic (u : ℕ → R) (c1 c2 : R)
    (h : ∀ k, u (k + 2) = c1 * u (k + 1) - c2 * u k) :
    PowerSeries.mk u * (1 - C c1 * X + C c2 * X ^ 2)
      = C (u 0) * X ^ 0 + C (u 1 - c1 * u 0) * X ^ 1 := by
  have expand : PowerSeries.mk u * (1 - C c1 * X + C c2 * X ^ 2)
      = PowerSeries.mk u * (C 1 * X ^ 0) - PowerSeries.mk u * (C c1 * X ^ 1)
        + PowerSeries.mk u * (C c2 * X ^ 2) := by
    simp [pow_zero, pow_one]; ring
  set A0 : R := u 0 with hA0
  set A1 : R := u 1 - c1 * u 0 with hA1
  ext m
  rw [expand]
  simp only [map_sub, map_add, coeff_mk_mul_CX, coeff_CX]
  match m with
  | 0 => simp [hA0]
  | 1 => simp [hA1]
  | (n + 2) =>
      have hn := h n
      simp only [show n + 2 - 1 = n + 1 from rfl, show n + 2 - 2 = n from rfl,
        show n + 2 - 0 = n + 2 from rfl]
      simp
      linear_combination hn

/-- Rationality of a local L-series attached to a degree-three linear recursion:
the GL(3) shape. -/
theorem mk_mul_cubic (u : ℕ → R) (c1 c2 c3 : R)
    (h : ∀ k, u (k + 3) = c1 * u (k + 2) - c2 * u (k + 1) + c3 * u k) :
    PowerSeries.mk u * (1 - C c1 * X + C c2 * X ^ 2 - C c3 * X ^ 3)
      = C (u 0) * X ^ 0 + C (u 1 - c1 * u 0) * X ^ 1
        + C (u 2 - c1 * u 1 + c2 * u 0) * X ^ 2 := by
  have expand : PowerSeries.mk u * (1 - C c1 * X + C c2 * X ^ 2 - C c3 * X ^ 3)
      = PowerSeries.mk u * (C 1 * X ^ 0) - PowerSeries.mk u * (C c1 * X ^ 1)
        + PowerSeries.mk u * (C c2 * X ^ 2) - PowerSeries.mk u * (C c3 * X ^ 3) := by
    simp [pow_zero, pow_one]; ring
  set A0 : R := u 0 with hA0
  set A1 : R := u 1 - c1 * u 0 with hA1
  set A2 : R := u 2 - c1 * u 1 + c2 * u 0 with hA2
  ext m
  rw [expand]
  simp only [map_sub, map_add, coeff_mk_mul_CX, coeff_CX]
  match m with
  | 0 => simp [hA0]
  | 1 => simp [hA1]
  | 2 => simp [hA2]
  | (n + 3) =>
      have hn := h n
      simp only [show n + 3 - 1 = n + 2 from rfl, show n + 3 - 2 = n + 1 from rfl,
        show n + 3 - 3 = n from rfl, show n + 3 - 0 = n + 3 from rfl]
      simp
      linear_combination hn

/-- Rationality of a local L-series attached to a degree-four linear recursion:
the GL(4) shape. -/
theorem mk_mul_quartic (u : ℕ → R) (c1 c2 c3 c4 : R)
    (h : ∀ k, u (k + 4) = c1 * u (k + 3) - c2 * u (k + 2) + c3 * u (k + 1) - c4 * u k) :
    PowerSeries.mk u * (1 - C c1 * X + C c2 * X ^ 2 - C c3 * X ^ 3 + C c4 * X ^ 4)
      = C (u 0) * X ^ 0 + C (u 1 - c1 * u 0) * X ^ 1
        + C (u 2 - c1 * u 1 + c2 * u 0) * X ^ 2
        + C (u 3 - c1 * u 2 + c2 * u 1 - c3 * u 0) * X ^ 3 := by
  have expand : PowerSeries.mk u * (1 - C c1 * X + C c2 * X ^ 2 - C c3 * X ^ 3 + C c4 * X ^ 4)
      = PowerSeries.mk u * (C 1 * X ^ 0) - PowerSeries.mk u * (C c1 * X ^ 1)
        + PowerSeries.mk u * (C c2 * X ^ 2) - PowerSeries.mk u * (C c3 * X ^ 3)
        + PowerSeries.mk u * (C c4 * X ^ 4) := by
    simp [pow_zero, pow_one]; ring
  set A0 : R := u 0 with hA0
  set A1 : R := u 1 - c1 * u 0 with hA1
  set A2 : R := u 2 - c1 * u 1 + c2 * u 0 with hA2
  set A3 : R := u 3 - c1 * u 2 + c2 * u 1 - c3 * u 0 with hA3
  ext m
  rw [expand]
  simp only [map_sub, map_add, coeff_mk_mul_CX, coeff_CX]
  match m with
  | 0 => simp [hA0]
  | 1 => simp [hA1]
  | 2 => simp [hA2]
  | 3 => simp [hA3]
  | (n + 4) =>
      have hn := h n
      simp only [show n + 4 - 1 = n + 3 from rfl, show n + 4 - 2 = n + 2 from rfl,
        show n + 4 - 3 = n + 1 from rfl, show n + 4 - 4 = n from rfl,
        show n + 4 - 0 = n + 4 from rfl]
      simp
      linear_combination hn

end PowerSeriesTools

# Future directions

Five falsifiable conjectures growing out of the formalisation in
`Catalog/Shared/Langlands*.lean` (local Satake theory of `GL(2)`, symmetric power liftings to
`GL(3)` and `GL(4)`, the general Clebsch–Gordan decomposition of `Sym^m × Sym^n`, and
temperedness transfer).

---

## C1. Full Clebsch–Gordan without the ordering hypothesis, in the `min` form

**Conjecture.** For all `m, n` (no hypothesis `n ≤ m`),
`∏_{i≤m}∏_{j≤n}(1 - γ^{(m)}_i γ^{(n)}_j X) = ∏_{r ≤ min(m,n)} ∏_{i ≤ m+n-2r}(1 - (ab)^r γ^{(m+n-2r)}_i X)`.

The key insight is that the whole statement is a *purely combinatorial* identity of multisets
of index sums — `prod_grid_eq` in `LanglandsGeneralClebschGordan.lean` proves exactly this in
an arbitrary commutative monoid for `n ≤ m` — so the general case only needs the symmetric
version of that grid lemma, with `min(m,n)` replacing `n`; the computational evidence in
`ComputationalEvidence.md` shows the naive `r ≤ n` bound genuinely fails for `n > m`, so the
`min` is essential and the conjecture is sharply falsifiable.

**Why now?** The `n ≤ m` case is fully proved and the missing step is a swap-symmetry argument
(`prod_grid_eq` is symmetric in `m, n` on the left-hand side), so the conjecture can be
settled without any new mathematical input, purely by strengthening one monoid-level lemma.

---

import Mathlib

/-!
# Langlands functoriality, I: Satake parameters, Hecke eigenvalues and local L-factors

This file develops, over an arbitrary commutative ring, the algebraic skeleton of the
local theory that underlies the Langlands program for `GL(2)`:

* the **Satake parameters** `(a, b)` of an unramified local representation of `GL(2)`;
* the associated **Hecke eigenvalue sequence** `hecke a b k` (the coefficient of the local
  L-function at `p ^ k`), defined by the classical degree-two recursion
  `a_{p^{k+2}} = a_p * a_{p^{k+1}} - χ(p) * a_{p^k}`;
* the **local L-function** as a formal power series, and the fact that it is the inverse of
  the degree-two Euler factor `(1 - a X)(1 - b X)`;
* the **Clebsch–Gordan / Hecke multiplicativity** identity
  `h_{n+d} * h_n = ∑_{i ≤ n} (ab)^{n-i} h_{d + 2i}`,
  which is the Satake-parameter shadow of the decomposition
  `Sym^m ⊗ Sym^n = ⊕_j Sym^{m+n-2j} ⊗ det^j`, and hence the local engine of functoriality;
* the **Ramanujan bound** `‖h_k‖ ≤ k + 1` for tempered (unitary) Satake parameters.

The general power-series lemma `PowerSeriesRecursion.mk_mul_eulerFactor` records the exact
equivalence "linear recursion of Hecke eigenvalues ↔ rationality of the local L-series with
prescribed Euler factor"; it is the workhorse for the `GL(3)` and `GL(4)` transfers in
`LanglandsSymmetricPower.lean`.
-/

namespace Langlands

open Finset PowerSeries

section PowerSeriesTools

variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R]

/-- Coefficient of `mk u * (C c * X ^ j)`: a shifted, scaled coefficient of `u`. -/
lemma coeff_mk_mul_CX (u : ℕ → R) (c : R) (j m : ℕ) :
    coeff m (PowerSeries.mk u * (C c * X ^ j)) = if j ≤ m then c * u (m - j) else 0 := by
  rw [show PowerSeries.mk u * (C c * X ^ j) = (C c * PowerSeries.mk u) * X ^ j by ring,
    coeff_mul_X_pow']
  split <;> simp

/-- Coefficient of a monomial `C a * X ^ j`. -/
lemma coeff_CX (a : R) (j m : ℕ) : coeff m (C a * X ^ j) = if m = j then a else 0 := by
  rw [coeff_C_mul, coeff_X_pow]; split <;> simp

/-- **Rationality from a linear recursion.**  If the sequence `u` satisfies the linear
recursion whose characteristic polynomial has coefficients `e 0, …, e d`, then the generating
series `∑ u k X ^ k` multiplied by the Euler factor `∑_{j ≤ d} e j X ^ j` is a polynomial of
degree `< d`, with explicitly computed coefficients.  This is the formal statement that a
local L-function is the reciprocal of a polynomial of degree `d`. -/
theorem mk_mul_eulerFactor (u : ℕ → R) (e : ℕ → R) (d : ℕ) (B : ℕ → R)
    (hB : ∀ m, B m = ∑ j ∈ range (m + 1), e j * u (m - j))
    (hrec : ∀ k, ∑ j ∈ range (d + 1), e j * u (k + d - j) = 0) :
    PowerSeries.mk u * (∑ j ∈ range (d + 1), C (e j) * X ^ j)
      = ∑ m ∈ range d, C (B m) * X ^ m := by
  ext m
  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  simp only [map_sum, coeff_mk_mul_CX, coeff_CX]
  by_cases hm : m < d
  · -- low-degree coefficients: both sides are the truncated convolution
    have hR : ∑ m' ∈ range d, (if m = m' then B m' else 0) = B m := by
      rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq (range d) m B, if_pos (Finset.mem_range.mpr hm)]
    have hL : ∑ j ∈ range (d + 1), (if j ≤ m then e j * u (m - j) else 0) = B m := by
      have hcast : ∀ j ∈ range (d + 1), (if j ≤ m then e j * u (m - j) else 0)
          = if j ∈ range (m + 1) then e j * u (m - j) else 0 := by
        intro j _
        simp
      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hcast, Finset.sum_ite_mem,
        Finset.inter_eq_right.mpr (by
          intro x hx
          simp only [Finset.mem_range] at hx ⊢
          omega), hB]
    rw [hL, hR]
  · -- high-degree coefficients: the recursion makes them vanish
    push_neg at hm
    have hzero : ∑ j ∈ range (d + 1), (if j ≤ m then e j * u (m - j) else 0) = 0 := by
      have hshift : ∀ j ∈ range (d + 1), (if j ≤ m then e j * u (m - j) else 0)
          = e j * u ((m - d) + d - j) := by
        intro j hj
        have hjd : j ≤ d := Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp (Finset.mem_range.mp hj)
        have hjm : j ≤ m := le_trans hjd hm
        rw [if_pos hjm, Nat.sub_add_cancel hm]
      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hshift]
      exact hrec (m - d)
    rw [hzero, Finset.sum_eq_zero]
    intro m' hm'
    have hne : ¬ (m = m') := by
      have := Finset.mem_range.mp hm'
      omega
    simp [hne]

/-- Rationality of a local L-series attached to a degree-two linear recursion. -/
theorem mk_mul_quadratic (u : ℕ → R) (c1 c2 : R)
    (h : ∀ k, u (k + 2) = c1 * u (k + 1) - c2 * u k) :
    PowerSeries.mk u * (1 - C c1 * X + C c2 * X ^ 2)
      = C (u 0) * X ^ 0 + C (u 1 - c1 * u 0) * X ^ 1 := by
  have expand : PowerSeries.mk u * (1 - C c1 * X + C c2 * X ^ 2)
      = PowerSeries.mk u * (C 1 * X ^ 0) - PowerSeries.mk u * (C c1 * X ^ 1)
        + PowerSeries.mk u * (C c2 * X ^ 2) := by
    simp [pow_zero, pow_one]; ring
  set A0 : R := u 0 with hA0
  set A1 : R := u 1 - c1 * u 0 with hA1
  ext m
  rw [expand]
  simp only [map_sub, map_add, coeff_mk_mul_CX, coeff_CX]
  match m with
  | 0 => simp [hA0]
  | 1 => simp [hA1]
  | (n + 2) =>
      have hn := h n
      simp only [show n + 2 - 1 = n + 1 from rfl, show n + 2 - 2 = n from rfl,
        show n + 2 - 0 = n + 2 from rfl]
      simp
      linear_combination hn

/-- Rationality of a local L-series attached to a degree-three linear recursion:
the GL(3) shape. -/
theorem mk_mul_cubic (u : ℕ → R) (c1 c2 c3 : R)
    (h : ∀ k, u (k + 3) = c1 * u (k + 2) - c2 * u (k + 1) + c3 * u k) :
    PowerSeries.mk u * (1 - C c1 * X + C c2 * X ^ 2 - C c3 * X ^ 3)
      = C (u 0) * X ^ 0 + C (u 1 - c1 * u 0) * X ^ 1
        + C (u 2 - c1 * u 1 + c2 * u 0) * X ^ 2 := by
  have expand : PowerSeries.mk u * (1 - C c1 * X + C c2 * X ^ 2 - C c3 * X ^ 3)
      = PowerSeries.mk u * (C 1 * X ^ 0) - PowerSeries.mk u * (C c1 * X ^ 1)
        + PowerSeries.mk u * (C c2 * X ^ 2) - PowerSeries.mk u * (C c3 * X ^ 3) := by
    simp [pow_zero, pow_one]; ring
  set A0 : R := u 0 with hA0
  set A1 : R := u 1 - c1 * u 0 with hA1
  set A2 : R := u 2 - c1 * u 1 + c2 * u 0 with hA2
  ext m
  rw [expand]
  simp only [map_sub, map_add, coeff_mk_mul_CX, coeff_CX]
  match m with
  | 0 => simp [hA0]
  | 1 => simp [hA1]
  | 2 => simp [hA2]
  | (n + 3) =>
      have hn := h n
      simp only [show n + 3 - 1 = n + 2 from rfl, show n + 3 - 2 = n + 1 from rfl,
        show n + 3 - 3 = n from rfl, show n + 3 - 0 = n + 3 from rfl]
      simp
      linear_combination hn

/-- Rationality of a local L-series attached to a degree-four linear recursion:
the GL(4) shape. -/
theorem mk_mul_quartic (u : ℕ → R) (c1 c2 c3 c4 : R)
    (h : ∀ k, u (k + 4) = c1 * u (k + 3) - c2 * u (k + 2) + c3 * u (k + 1) - c4 * u k) :
    PowerSeries.mk u * (1 - C c1 * X + C c2 * X ^ 2 - C c3 * X ^ 3 + C c4 * X ^ 4)
      = C (u 0) * X ^ 0 + C (u 1 - c1 * u 0) * X ^ 1
        + C (u 2 - c1 * u 1 + c2 * u 0) * X ^ 2
        + C (u 3 - c1 * u 2 + c2 * u 1 - c3 * u 0) * X ^ 3 := by
  have expand : PowerSeries.mk u * (1 - C c1 * X + C c2 * X ^ 2 - C c3 * X ^ 3 + C c4 * X ^ 4)
      = PowerSeries.mk u * (C 1 * X ^ 0) - PowerSeries.mk u * (C c1 * X ^ 1)
        + PowerSeries.mk u * (C c2 * X ^ 2) - PowerSeries.mk u * (C c3 * X ^ 3)
        + PowerSeries.mk u * (C c4 * X ^ 4) := by
    simp [pow_zero, pow_one]; ring
  set A0 : R := u 0 with hA0
  set A1 : R := u 1 - c1 * u 0 with hA1
  set A2 : R := u 2 - c1 * u 1 + c2 * u 0 with hA2
  set A3 : R := u 3 - c1 * u 2 + c2 * u 1 - c3 * u 0 with hA3
  ext m
  rw [expand]
  simp only [map_sub, map_add, coeff_mk_mul_CX, coeff_CX]
  match m with
  | 0 => simp [hA0]
  | 1 => simp [hA1]
  | 2 => simp [hA2]
  | 3 => simp [hA3]
  | (n + 4) =>
      have hn := h n
      simp only [show n + 4 - 1 = n + 3 from rfl, show n + 4 - 2 = n + 2 from rfl,
        show n + 4 - 3 = n + 1 from rfl, show n + 4 - 4 = n from rfl,
        show n + 4 - 0 = n + 4 from rfl]
      simp
      linear_combination hn

end PowerSeriesTools

section Hecke

variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R]

/-- The Hecke eigenvalue sequence attached to a pair of Satake parameters `(a, b)`:
`hecke a b k` is the coefficient of the local L-function of an unramified representation of
`GL(2)` at `p ^ k`, i.e. the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomial `h_k (a, b)`. -/
def hecke (a b : R) : ℕ → R
  | 0 => 1
  | 1 => a + b
  | (k + 2) => (a + b) * hecke a b (k + 1) - (a * b) * hecke a b k

@[simp] lemma hecke_zero (a b : R) : hecke a b 0 = 1 := rfl

@[simp] lemma hecke_one (a b : R) : hecke a b 1 = a + b := rfl

lemma hecke_add_two (a b : R) (k : ℕ) :
    hecke a b (k + 2) = (a + b) * hecke a b (k + 1) - (a * b) * hecke a b k := rfl

/-- The Hecke relation in the form `a_p · a_{p^{k+1}} = a_{p^{k+2}} + χ(p) · a_{p^k}`. -/
lemma hecke_mul_hecke_one (a b : R) (k : ℕ) :
    hecke a b 1 * hecke a b (k + 1) = hecke a b (k + 2) + (a * b) * hecke a b k := by
  rw [hecke_add_two, hecke_one]; ring

/-- **Master identity.**  For all `n, d`:
`h_{n+d+1} h_{n+1} = (ab) · h_{n+d} h_n + h_{2n+d+2}`.
This single two-parameter identity contains every Clebsch–Gordan relation for the
Satake parameters of `GL(2)`; the proof is an induction on `n` with `d` universally
quantified, feeding the inductive hypothesis back at both `d` and `d + 1`. -/
theorem hecke_master (a b : R) : ∀ n d : ℕ,
    hecke a b (n + d + 1) * hecke a b (n + 1)
      = (a * b) * (hecke a b (n + d) * hecke a b n) + hecke a b (2 * n + d + 2) := by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero =>
      intro d
      have h := hecke_add_two a b d
      simp only [Nat.zero_add, hecke_zero, hecke_one, mul_one]
      rw [show 2 * 0 + d + 2 = d + 2 by ring]
      rw [h]; ring
  | succ n ih =>
      intro d
      have i1 := ih (d + 1)
      have i2 := ih d
      have r1 := hecke_add_two a b n
      have r2 := hecke_add_two a b (n + d)
      have r3 := hecke_add_two a b (2 * n + d + 2)
      rw [show n + 1 + d + 1 = n + d + 2 by ring, show n + 1 + 1 = n + 2 by ring,
        show n + 1 + d = n + d + 1 by ring, show 2 * (n + 1) + d + 2 = 2 * n + d + 4 by ring]
      rw [show n + (d + 1) + 1 = n + d + 2 by ring, show n + (d + 1) = n + d + 1 by ring,
        show 2 * n + (d + 1) + 2 = 2 * n + d + 3 by ring] at i1
      rw [show n + d + 2 = n + d + 2 from rfl] at r2
      rw [show 2 * n + d + 2 + 2 = 2 * n + d + 4 by ring,
        show 2 * n + d + 2 + 1 = 2 * n + d + 3 by ring] at r3
      rw [show n + d + 1 + 1 = n + d + 2 by ring] at r2
      linear_combination (hecke a b (n + d + 2)) * r1 - r3 + (a + b) * i1 - (a * b) * i2
        - (a * b) * hecke a b n * r2

/-- **Clebsch–Gordan for Satake parameters** (Hecke multiplicativity).
`h_{n+d} · h_n = ∑_{i=0}^{n} (ab)^{n-i} h_{d + 2i}`.

This is the local avatar of `Sym^{n+d} ⊗ Sym^n = ⊕_{i=0}^{n} Sym^{d+2i} ⊗ det^{n-i}`,
i.e. of the Rankin–Selberg decomposition of a product of two Hecke eigenvalues. -/
theorem hecke_clebsch_gordan (a b : R) : ∀ n d : ℕ,
    hecke a b (n + d) * hecke a b n
      = ∑ i ∈ range (n + 1), (a * b) ^ (n - i) * hecke a b (d + 2 * i) := by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero => intro d; simp
  | succ n ih =>
      intro d
      have hm := hecke_master a b n d
      rw [show n + 1 + d = n + d + 1 by ring]
      rw [hm, ih d, Finset.mul_sum,
        Finset.sum_range_succ (f := fun i => (a * b) ^ (n + 1 - i) * hecke a b (d + 2 * i)) (n := n + 1)]
      have hstep : ∀ i ∈ range (n + 1),
          (a * b) * ((a * b) ^ (n - i) * hecke a b (d + 2 * i))
            = (a * b) ^ (n + 1 - i) * hecke a b (d + 2 * i) := by
        intro i hi
        have hin : i ≤ n := Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp (Finset.mem_range.mp hi)
        rw [← mul_assoc, ← pow_succ']
        congr 2
        omega
      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hstep]
      congr 1
      rw [show n + 1 - (n + 1) = 0 by omega, pow_zero, one_mul]
      congr 1
      omega

/-- The Hecke square identity `h_{n+1}^2 - (ab) h_n^2 = h_{2n+2}`, the `d = 0` case of the
master identity.  It is the local Rankin–Selberg relation `a_{p^n}^2 = ∑_j χ(p)^j a_{p^{2n-2j}}`
in telescoped form. -/
theorem hecke_sq_sub (a b : R) (n : ℕ) :
    hecke a b (n + 1) ^ 2 - (a * b) * hecke a b n ^ 2 = hecke a b (2 * n + 2) := by
  have h := hecke_master a b n 0
  simp only [Nat.add_zero] at h
  linear_combination h

/-- Two-step recursion for the even-indexed Hecke eigenvalues: they are the Hecke
eigenvalues of the Satake pair `(a^2, b^2)`. -/
theorem hecke_even_rec (a b : R) (m : ℕ) :
    hecke a b (m + 4) = (a ^ 2 + b ^ 2) * hecke a b (m + 2) - (a * b) ^ 2 * hecke a b m := by
  have r1 := hecke_add_two a b (m + 2)
  have r2 := hecke_add_two a b (m + 1)
  have r3 := hecke_add_two a b m
  rw [show m + 2 + 2 = m + 4 by ring, show m + 2 + 1 = m + 3 by ring] at r1
  rw [show m + 1 + 2 = m + 3 by ring, show m + 1 + 1 = m + 2 by ring] at r2
  linear_combination r1 + (a + b) * r2 + (a * b) * r3

end Hecke

section LSeries

variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R]

/-- The local L-series of the unramified `GL(2)`-representation with Satake parameters
`(a, b)`: the generating series `∑ a_{p^k} X^k`. -/
noncomputable def L2 (a b : R) : PowerSeries R := mk (hecke a b)

/-- The geometric series `∑ c^k X^k`, i.e. the local L-function of a `GL(1)` character. -/
noncomputable def L1 (c : R) : PowerSeries R := mk fun k => c ^ k

/-- The `GL(1)` local L-function inverts its Euler factor. -/
theorem L1_mul_euler (c : R) : L1 c * (1 - C c * X) = 1 := by
  ext n
  cases n with
  | zero => simp [L1]
  | succ m => simp [L1, mul_sub, mul_comm, mul_left_comm, pow_succ]

/-- **The GL(2) local L-function inverts the degree-two Euler factor.**
`(∑_k a_{p^k} X^k) · (1 - a X)(1 - b X) = 1`. -/
theorem L2_mul_euler (a b : R) : L2 a b * ((1 - C a * X) * (1 - C b * X)) = 1 := by
  have key := mk_mul_quadratic (hecke a b) (a + b) (a * b) (fun k => hecke_add_two a b k)
  rw [show (1 - C a * X) * (1 - C b * X) = 1 - C (a + b) * X + C (a * b) * X ^ 2 by
    rw [map_add, map_mul]; ring]
  rw [L2, key]
  simp

/-- Inverses in a commutative power series ring are unique. -/
lemma inv_unique {f g e : PowerSeries R} (hf : f * e = 1) (hg : g * e = 1) : f = g := by
  calc f = f * (e * g) := by rw [mul_comm e g, hg, mul_one]
  _ = (f * e) * g := by ring
  _ = g := by rw [hf, one_mul]

/-- **Factorisation of the GL(2) local L-function into GL(1) factors.**
`L(π, X) = L(a, X) · L(b, X)`; equivalently the Hecke eigenvalues are the complete
homogeneous symmetric functions of the Satake parameters. -/
theorem L2_eq_L1_mul_L1 (a b : R) : L2 a b = L1 a * L1 b := by
  refine inv_unique (e := (1 - C a * X) * (1 - C b * X)) (L2_mul_euler a b) ?_
  calc L1 a * L1 b * ((1 - C a * X) * (1 - C b * X))
      = (L1 a * (1 - C a * X)) * (L1 b * (1 - C b * X)) := by ring
    _ = 1 := by rw [L1_mul_euler, L1_mul_euler, mul_one]

/-- **Closed form for the Hecke eigenvalues**: `a_{p^k} = ∑_{i+j=k} a^i b^j`. -/
theorem hecke_eq_antidiagonal_sum (a b : R) (k : ℕ) :
    hecke a b k = ∑ ij ∈ Finset.antidiagonal k, a ^ ij.1 * b ^ ij.2 := by
  have h := congrArg (fun f => coeff k f) (L2_eq_L1_mul_L1 a b)
  simpa [L2, L1, coeff_mul] using h

/-- **Closed form, single-index version**: `a_{p^k} = ∑_{i=0}^{k} a^i b^{k-i}`. -/
theorem hecke_eq_sum_range (a b : R) (k : ℕ) :
    hecke a b k = ∑ i ∈ range (k + 1), a ^ i * b ^ (k - i) := by
  rw [hecke_eq_antidiagonal_sum, Finset.Nat.sum_antidiagonal_eq_sum_range_succ
    (f := fun i j => a ^ i * b ^ j)]

end LSeries

/-- **Ramanujan–Petersson bound at a tempered place.**  If the Satake parameters are unitary

/-- The degree-three Euler factor of an unramified `GL(3)` representation. -/
noncomputable def gl3Euler (c1 c2 c3 : R) : PowerSeries R :=
  1 - C c1 * X + C c2 * X ^ 2 - C c3 * X ^ 3

/-- The Hecke eigenvalue sequence of an unramified `GL(3)` representation with Satake
elementary symmetric data `(c1, c2, c3)`. -/
def hecke3 (c1 c2 c3 : R) : ℕ → R
  | 0 => 1
  | 1 => c1
  | 2 => c1 ^ 2 - c2
  | (k + 3) => c1 * hecke3 c1 c2 c3 (k + 2) - c2 * hecke3 c1 c2 c3 (k + 1)
      + c3 * hecke3 c1 c2 c3 k

@[simp] lemma hecke3_zero (c1 c2 c3 : R) : hecke3 c1 c2 c3 0 = 1 := rfl
@[simp] lemma hecke3_one (c1 c2 c3 : R) : hecke3 c1 c2 c3 1 = c1 := rfl
@[simp] lemma hecke3_two (c1 c2 c3 : R) : hecke3 c1 c2 c3 2 = c1 ^ 2 - c2 := rfl

lemma hecke3_add_three (c1 c2 c3 : R) (k : ℕ) :
    hecke3 c1 c2 c3 (k + 3) = c1 * hecke3 c1 c2 c3 (k + 2) - c2 * hecke3 c1 c2 c3 (k + 1)
      + c3 * hecke3 c1 c2 c3 k := rfl

/-- The GL(3) L-series inverts the GL(3) Euler factor. -/
theorem hecke3_L_mul_euler (c1 c2 c3 : R) :
    PowerSeries.mk (hecke3 c1 c2 c3) * gl3Euler c1 c2 c3 = 1 := by
  rw [gl3Euler, mk_mul_cubic _ c1 c2 c3 (fun k => hecke3_add_three c1 c2 c3 k)]
  have e1 : hecke3 c1 c2 c3 1 - c1 * hecke3 c1 c2 c3 0 = 0 := by
    rw [hecke3_zero, hecke3_one]; ring
  have e2 : hecke3 c1 c2 c3 2 - c1 * hecke3 c1 c2 c3 1 + c2 * hecke3 c1 c2 c3 0 = 0 := by
    rw [hecke3_zero, hecke3_one, hecke3_two]; ring
  rw [e1, e2, hecke3_zero]
  simp

/-- Congruence lemma for the GL(3) Euler factor. -/
lemma gl3Euler_congr {c1 c2 c3 d1 d2 d3 : R} (h1 : c1 = d1) (h2 : c2 = d2) (h3 : c3 = d3) :
    gl3Euler c1 c2 c3 = gl3Euler d1 d2 d3 := by rw [h1, h2, h3]

/-- Expansion of a product of three linear Euler factors. -/
lemma euler_three_expand (x y z : R) :
    (1 - C x * X) * (1 - C y * X) * (1 - C z * X)
      = gl3Euler (x + y + z) (x * y + y * z + z * x) (x * y * z) := by
  rw [gl3Euler]
  simp only [map_add, map_mul]
  ring

lemma hecke_two_eq (a b : R) : hecke a b 2 = a ^ 2 + a * b + b ^ 2 := by
  rw [hecke_add_two]; simp; ring

/-- **The Gelbart–Jacquet Euler factor.**  The degree-three Euler polynomial of `Sym^2 π`
has coefficients that are explicit polynomials in the `GL(2)` Hecke data:
the `p`-th coefficient of the lift is `a_p^2 - χ(p) = a_{p^2}`, the second is
`χ(p) · a_{p^2}` and the determinant is `χ(p)^3`. -/
theorem symEuler_two_eq (a b : R) :
    symEuler 2 a b
      = gl3Euler (hecke a b 2) ((a * b) * hecke a b 2) ((a * b) ^ 3) := by
  rw [symEuler]
  rw [Finset.prod_range_succ, Finset.prod_range_succ, Finset.prod_range_one]
  have h0 : symSatake 2 a b 0 = b ^ 2 := by simp [symSatake]
  have h1 : symSatake 2 a b 1 = a * b := by simp [symSatake]
  have h2 : symSatake 2 a b 2 = a ^ 2 := by simp [symSatake]
  rw [h0, h1, h2, euler_three_expand, hecke_two_eq]
  exact gl3Euler_congr (by ring) (by ring) (by ring)

/-- The `p`-th Hecke eigenvalue of the Gelbart–Jacquet lift is `a_p^2 - χ(p)`. -/
theorem gelbart_jacquet_eigenvalue (a b : R) :
    hecke a b 2 = hecke a b 1 ^ 2 - a * b := by
  rw [hecke_two_eq, hecke_one]; ring

/-- **Gelbart–Jacquet transfer (local form).**  The L-factor of the symmetric square lift of
`π` coincides with the L-factor of the unramified `GL(3)` representation whose Hecke
eigenvalues obey the three-term recursion with data
`(a_p^2 - χ(p), χ(p)(a_p^2 - χ(p)), χ(p)^3)`.  In particular the Dirichlet coefficients of
`L(s, Sym^2 π)` are the `GL(3)` Hecke eigenvalues `hecke3`. -/
theorem gelbart_jacquet (a b : R) :
    symL 2 a b
      = PowerSeries.mk (hecke3 (hecke a b 2) ((a * b) * hecke a b 2) ((a * b) ^ 3)) := by
  refine inv_unique (e := symEuler 2 a b) (symL_mul_symEuler 2 a b) ?_
  rw [symEuler_two_eq]
  exact hecke3_L_mul_euler _ _ _

/-- Self-duality of the Gelbart–Jacquet lift for trivial central character: the GL(3) Euler
polynomial is palindromic, `1 - c X + c X^2 - X^3`. -/
theorem symEuler_two_selfdual (a b : R) (hab : a * b = 1) :
    symEuler 2 a b = gl3Euler (hecke a b 2) (hecke a b 2) 1 := by
  rw [symEuler_two_eq, hab, one_mul, one_pow]

end GL3

section RankinSelberg

variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R]

/-- The squares of the Hecke eigenvalues satisfy the `GL(3)` three-term recursion attached to
the symmetric square Satake data.  This is the local Rankin–Selberg phenomenon:
`L(s, π × π)` is, up to the factor `1 + χ(p)X`, a `GL(3)` L-function. -/
theorem hecke_sq_rec (a b : R) (k : ℕ) :
    hecke a b (k + 3) ^ 2
      = hecke a b 2 * hecke a b (k + 2) ^ 2 - ((a * b) * hecke a b 2) * hecke a b (k + 1) ^ 2
        + (a * b) ^ 3 * hecke a b k ^ 2 := by
  have d0 := hecke_sq_sub a b k
  have d1 := hecke_sq_sub a b (k + 1)
  have d2 := hecke_sq_sub a b (k + 2)
  have e := hecke_even_rec a b (2 * k + 2)
  rw [show 2 * (k + 1) + 2 = 2 * k + 4 by ring] at d1
  rw [show 2 * (k + 2) + 2 = 2 * k + 6 by ring] at d2
  rw [show 2 * k + 2 + 4 = 2 * k + 6 by ring, show 2 * k + 2 + 2 = 2 * k + 4 by ring] at e
  rw [hecke_two_eq]
  linear_combination d2 + e - (a ^ 2 + b ^ 2) * d1 + (a * b) ^ 2 * d0

/-- **Local Rankin–Selberg identity.**
`(∑_k a_{p^k}^2 X^k) · L(Sym^2 π, X)^{-1} = 1 + χ(p) X`, i.e.
`L(s, π × π) = (1 + χ(p) p^{-s}) · L(s, Sym^2 π)` locally at `p`.
Equivalently `L(s, π × π) = ζ_p(s) L(s, Sym^2 π) / ζ_p(2s)` in the classical normalisation. -/
theorem rankin_selberg_sym_two (a b : R) :
    PowerSeries.mk (fun k => hecke a b k ^ 2) * symEuler 2 a b = 1 + C (a * b) * X := by
  rw [symEuler_two_eq, gl3Euler]
  rw [mk_mul_cubic (fun k => hecke a b k ^ 2) (hecke a b 2) ((a * b) * hecke a b 2)
      ((a * b) ^ 3) (fun k => hecke_sq_rec a b k)]
  have hC : (C (hecke a b 2) : PowerSeries R) = C a ^ 2 + C a * C b + C b ^ 2 := by
    rw [hecke_two_eq]
    simp only [map_add, map_mul, map_pow]
  simp only [hecke_zero, hecke_one, map_sub, map_add, map_mul, map_pow, map_one,
    pow_zero, pow_one, mul_one]
  rw [hC]
  ring

end RankinSelberg

section GL4

variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R]

/-- The degree-four Euler factor of an unramified `GL(4)` representation. -/
noncomputable def gl4Euler (c1 c2 c3 c4 : R) : PowerSeries R :=
  1 - C c1 * X + C c2 * X ^ 2 - C c3 * X ^ 3 + C c4 * X ^ 4

/-- The Hecke eigenvalue sequence of an unramified `GL(4)` representation. -/
def hecke4 (c1 c2 c3 c4 : R) : ℕ → R
  | 0 => 1
  | 1 => c1
  | 2 => c1 ^ 2 - c2
  | 3 => c1 ^ 3 - 2 * c1 * c2 + c3
  | (k + 4) => c1 * hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4 (k + 3) - c2 * hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4 (k + 2)
      + c3 * hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4 (k + 1) - c4 * hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4 k

lemma hecke4_add_four (c1 c2 c3 c4 : R) (k : ℕ) :
    hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4 (k + 4) = c1 * hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4 (k + 3) - c2 * hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4 (k + 2)
      + c3 * hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4 (k + 1) - c4 * hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4 k := rfl

/-- The GL(4) L-series inverts the GL(4) Euler factor. -/
theorem hecke4_L_mul_euler (c1 c2 c3 c4 : R) :
    PowerSeries.mk (hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4) * gl4Euler c1 c2 c3 c4 = 1 := by
  rw [gl4Euler, mk_mul_quartic _ c1 c2 c3 c4 (fun k => hecke4_add_four c1 c2 c3 c4 k)]
  show (C ((hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4) 0) * X ^ 0 + C ((hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4) 1 - c1 * (hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4) 0) * X ^ 1
      + C ((hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4) 2 - c1 * (hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4) 1 + c2 * (hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4) 0) * X ^ 2
      + C ((hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4) 3 - c1 * (hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4) 2 + c2 * (hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4) 1
          - c3 * (hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4) 0) * X ^ 3) = 1
  have e0 : (hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4) 0 = 1 := rfl
  have e1 : (hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4) 1 = c1 := rfl
  have e2 : (hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4) 2 = c1 ^ 2 - c2 := rfl
  have e3 : (hecke4 c1 c2 c3 c4) 3 = c1 ^ 3 - 2 * c1 * c2 + c3 := rfl
  rw [e0, e1, e2, e3]
  have z1 : (c1 : R) - c1 * 1 = 0 := by ring
  have z2 : (c1 : R) ^ 2 - c2 - c1 * c1 + c2 * 1 = 0 := by ring
  have z3 : (c1 : R) ^ 3 - 2 * c1 * c2 + c3 - c1 * (c1 ^ 2 - c2) + c2 * c1 - c3 * 1 = 0 := by ring
  rw [z1, z2, z3]
  simp

/-- Congruence lemma for the GL(4) Euler factor. -/
lemma gl4Euler_congr {c1 c2 c3 c4 d1 d2 d3 d4 : R} (h1 : c1 = d1) (h2 : c2 = d2) (h3 : c3 = d3)
    (h4 : c4 = d4) : gl4Euler c1 c2 c3 c4 = gl4Euler d1 d2 d3 d4 := by rw [h1, h2, h3, h4]

/-- Expansion of a product of four linear Euler factors. -/
lemma euler_four_expand (w x y z : R) :
    (1 - C w * X) * (1 - C x * X) * (1 - C y * X) * (1 - C z * X)
      = gl4Euler (w + x + y + z)
          (w * x + w * y + w * z + x * y + x * z + y * z)
          (w * x * y + w * x * z + w * y * z + x * y * z) (w * x * y * z) := by
  rw [gl4Euler]
  simp only [map_add, map_mul]
  ring

lemma hecke_three_eq (a b : R) : hecke a b 3 = a ^ 3 + a ^ 2 * b + a * b ^ 2 + b ^ 3 := by
  rw [hecke_add_two, hecke_two_eq]; simp; ring

lemma hecke_four_eq (a b : R) :
    hecke a b 4 = a ^ 4 + a ^ 3 * b + a ^ 2 * b ^ 2 + a * b ^ 3 + b ^ 4 := by
  rw [show (4 : ℕ) = 2 + 2 from rfl, hecke_add_two, hecke_three_eq, hecke_two_eq]
  ring

/-- **The symmetric cube Euler factor.**  The degree-four Euler polynomial of `Sym^3 π` has
coefficients expressed through the `GL(2)` Hecke eigenvalues:
`(a_{p^3}, χ(p)(a_{p^4} + χ(p)^2), χ(p)^3 a_{p^3}, χ(p)^6)`. -/
theorem symEuler_three_eq (a b : R) :
    symEuler 3 a b
      = gl4Euler (hecke a b 3) ((a * b) * (hecke a b 4 + (a * b) ^ 2))
          ((a * b) ^ 3 * hecke a b 3) ((a * b) ^ 6) := by
  rw [symEuler]
  rw [Finset.prod_range_succ, Finset.prod_range_succ, Finset.prod_range_succ,
    Finset.prod_range_one]
  have h0 : symSatake 3 a b 0 = b ^ 3 := by simp [symSatake]
  have h1 : symSatake 3 a b 1 = a * b ^ 2 := by simp [symSatake]
  have h2 : symSatake 3 a b 2 = a ^ 2 * b := by simp [symSatake]
  have h3 : symSatake 3 a b 3 = a ^ 3 := by simp [symSatake]
  rw [h0, h1, h2, h3, euler_four_expand, hecke_three_eq, hecke_four_eq]
  exact gl4Euler_congr (by ring) (by ring) (by ring) (by ring)

/-- **Symmetric cube transfer (local form).**  The L-factor of `Sym^3 π` is the L-factor of
the unramified `GL(4)` representation whose Hecke eigenvalues obey the four-term recursion
with the explicit `GL(2)` data. -/
theorem symcube_transfer (a b : R) :
    symL 3 a b
      = PowerSeries.mk (hecke4 (hecke a b 3) ((a * b) * (hecke a b 4 + (a * b) ^ 2))
          ((a * b) ^ 3 * hecke a b 3) ((a * b) ^ 6)) := by
  refine inv_unique (e := symEuler 3 a b) (symL_mul_symEuler 3 a b) ?_
  rw [symEuler_three_eq]
  exact hecke4_L_mul_euler _ _ _ _

end GL4

section Transfer

variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R]

lemma constantCoeff_L1 (c : R) : constantCoeff (L1 c) = 1 := by
  simp [L1]

lemma constantCoeff_prod_L1 (γ : ℕ → R) (n : ℕ) :
    constantCoeff (∏ i ∈ range n, L1 (γ i)) = 1 := by
  rw [map_prod]
  exact Finset.prod_eq_one fun i _ => constantCoeff_L1 (γ i)

lemma coeff_one_L1 (c : R) : coeff 1 (L1 c) = c := by
  simp [L1]

/-- The linear (i.e. `p`-th) Dirichlet coefficient of a product of `GL(1)` L-factors is the
sum of the corresponding Satake parameters. -/
lemma coeff_one_prod_L1 (γ : ℕ → R) (n : ℕ) :
    coeff 1 (∏ i ∈ range n, L1 (γ i)) = ∑ i ∈ range n, γ i := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
      rw [Finset.prod_range_succ, Finset.sum_range_succ, coeff_mul]
      rw [Finset.Nat.sum_antidiagonal_eq_sum_range_succ_mk]
      rw [Finset.sum_range_succ, Finset.sum_range_one]
      have hc : (coeff 0) (∏ i ∈ range n, L1 (γ i)) = 1 := by
        rw [PowerSeries.coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff]
        exact constantCoeff_prod_L1 γ n
      rw [hc, ih]
      simp [L1]
      ring

/-- **Transfer of Hecke eigenvalues.**  The `p`-th Hecke eigenvalue of the symmetric power
lift `Sym^n π` is the complete homogeneous symmetric function `h_n(a, b) = a_{p^n}`:
the functorial lift sends `a_p ↦ a_{p^n}`. -/
theorem symL_coeff_one (n : ℕ) (a b : R) :
    coeff 1 (symL n a b) = hecke a b n := by
  rw [symL, coeff_one_prod_L1, hecke_eq_sum_range]
  rfl

end Transfer

section Temperedness

/-- Unitarity of the `GL(2)` Satake parameters propagates to every symmetric power lift. -/
theorem symSatake_norm (n : ℕ) (a b : ℂ) (ha : ‖a‖ = 1) (hb : ‖b‖ = 1) (i : ℕ) :
    ‖symSatake n a b i‖ = 1 := by
  rw [symSatake, norm_mul, norm_pow, norm_pow, ha, hb, one_pow, one_pow, one_mul]

/-- **Functoriality preserves temperedness.**  If `π` satisfies the Ramanujan bound at `p`
(unitary Satake parameters), then the `p`-th Hecke eigenvalue of `Sym^n π` is bounded by
`n + 1`, the trivial bound for a tempered representation of `GL(n+1)`. -/
theorem sym_tempered (n : ℕ) (a b : ℂ) (ha : ‖a‖ = 1) (hb : ‖b‖ = 1) :
    ‖coeff 1 (symL n a b)‖ ≤ n + 1 := by
  rw [symL_coeff_one]
  exact hecke_norm_le a b ha hb n

/-- The Gelbart–Jacquet lift of a tempered representation is tempered at `p`:
`|a_p^2 - χ(p)| ≤ 3`. -/
theorem gelbart_jacquet_tempered (a b : ℂ) (ha : ‖a‖ = 1) (hb : ‖b‖ = 1) :
    ‖hecke a b 1 ^ 2 - a * b‖ ≤ 3 := by
  have h := hecke_norm_le a b ha hb 2
  rw [gelbart_jacquet_eigenvalue] at h
  norm_num at h
  exact h

end Temperedness

# Langlands functoriality, III: tensor transfer and Ramanujan bounds for the lifts

This file proves two families of results that go beyond the individual liftings of
`Shared.LanglandsSymmetricPower`.

## Tensor (Rankin–Selberg) functoriality in arbitrary symmetric power degree

`symEuler_tensor_one` and `symL_tensor_one` prove, for **every** `m`, the local
Rankin–Selberg factorisation

`L(Sym^m π × π, X) = L(Sym^{m+1} π, X) · L(Sym^{m-1} π ⊗ χ, X)`,

i.e. the functorial decomposition `Sym^m ⊗ Sym^1 = Sym^{m+1} ⊕ (Sym^{m-1} ⊗ det)` realised
on Satake parameters, Euler factors and Dirichlet coefficients.  The `m = 1` case is the
Gelbart–Jacquet identity `L(π × π) = L(Sym^2 π) L(χ)` already visible in
`rankin_selberg_sym_two`.

`hecke3_eq_prod` identifies the abstract `GL(3)` Hecke eigenvalues with the complete
homogeneous symmetric functions of the three Satake parameters, and `symL_two_coeff_norm_le`
deduces the full Ramanujan bound `|b_{p^k}| ≤ (k+1)(k+2)/2` for **all** powers of `p` for the

namespace Langlands

open Finset PowerSeries

section TensorTransfer

variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R]

lemma satake_mul_a (m : ℕ) (a b : R) (i : ℕ) :
    a * symSatake m a b i = symSatake (m + 1) a b (i + 1) := by
  rw [symSatake, symSatake, show m + 1 - (i + 1) = m - i by omega]
  ring

lemma satake_mul_b (m : ℕ) (a b : R) (i : ℕ) (hi : i ≤ m) :
    b * symSatake m a b i = symSatake (m + 1) a b i := by
  rw [symSatake, symSatake, show m + 1 - i = (m - i) + 1 by omega, pow_succ]

  rw [symSatake, symSatake, show m + 1 - (j + 1) = (m - 1 - j) + 1 by omega, pow_succ, pow_succ]

    intro j hj

    refine Finset.prod_eq_one ?_
    intro i _
